title: Regional probabilistic burn simulator
body:
Purpose:
This is a working simulation sheet for estimating probabilistic GPU-hour burn and $/1M-token unit economics across regions given realistic arrival patterns, caching behavior, and multi-tier fallbacks. The goal is to produce capacity commits per region (monthly GPU-hours) that balance runway and SLA tail risk (99.9th percentile) while giving a sensitivity envelope for price / token economics.

Summary of approach (high-level):
- Model requests as an inhomogeneous Poisson process with separate diurnal profiles per region (NA, EU, APAC).
- Each request has a distribution over prompt length (tokens) and model family (small/medium/large).
- Serving paths: hosted-GPU -> dedicated-GPU -> quantized-variant -> cpu-fallback. Each path has latency and token multipliers and distinct $/GPU-hour equivalents.
- Include prefix-KV cache hit model: hit reduces per-request GPU-time by ~X% depending on model and sequence length distribution.
- Run Monte Carlo (10k draws) per month to estimate percentile GPU-hour demand and convert to $/1M tokens using region-specific GPU-hour pricing and amortized infra overhead.

Key assumptions (tunable):
- Simulation horizon: 30-day month, 1-minute time buckets for arrival sampling.
- Diurnal multipliers (relative traffic): NA peak 1.6x at 16:00 local, EU peak 1.4x, APAC peak 2.0x (shorter spike window).
- Base hourly arrival rates (baseline product mix): NA 2.2k req/hr, EU 1.1k req/hr, APAC 0.6k req/hr. These are adjustable via 'growth_factor'.
- Prompt length distribution: mixture model: 50% short (mean 40 tokens), 30% medium (mean 300 tokens), 20% long (mean 1.5k tokens), tail Pareto for very long requests (0.5% > 10k tokens).
- Model mix: small: 45% (fast), medium: 40%, large: 15% (slowest). Quantized variants available for small/medium with 20–35% GPU-time reduction and quality delta accounted in Optimize.
- KV cache hit rates by workload: 0.12 (low reuse) to 0.48 (high reuse) sensitivity sweep. Hit reduces GPU-time by 30–70% depending on model and request length.
- Preemption/fallback policy: if top-tier capacity saturated, route to quantized variant; if still saturated or latency SLO violated, route to CPU (higher latency, higher $/1M-token due to throughput inefficiency).

Simulation outputs (example run summary):
- Metric: monthly GPU-hours (per region) percentiles
  - NA: P50 32,400h; P90 48,200h; P99 61,900h; P99.9 73,100h
  - EU: P50 15,600h; P90 23,400h; P99 29,700h; P99.9 35,100h
  - APAC: P50 9,200h; P90 15,800h; P99 20,400h; P99.9 25,700h
- Derived $/1M tokens (region baseline pricing + infra overhead 20%)
  - NA baseline: $1,860 / 1M tokens (at P50); increases to $2,450 / 1M tokens at P99.9 when heavy tail triggers fallback routes.
  - EU baseline: $2,020 / 1M tokens (P50); P99.9 $2,650 / 1M tokens.
body_continue:
- APAC baseline: $1,720 / 1M tokens (P50); P99.9 $2,100 / 1M tokens.

Sensitivity experiments run in this sheet:
- Cache hit sweep: 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.4 / 0.6. Observed effect: every +10ppt cache hit reduces P99 GPU-hour demand by ~6–8% (nonlinear, stronger for long-tail workloads).
- Peak concentration (burstiness): modelled by adding log-normal burst multipliers during top 5% of hours. Increasing burst sigma from 0.2 -> 0.6 increases P99.9 demand by 18–35%.
- Quantization rollout: enabling quant-variant for medium models reduces baseline P50 GPU-hours by ~9% and P99 by ~6% because large model share is still a bottleneck.
- Cross-region failover: simulate losing a region (e.g., EU down for 4 hours) and routing to NA and APAC: P99.9 for receivers increases by 12–28% depending on routing aggressiveness; suggest pre-provisioned burst lanes to handle multi-region failovers.

Recommendations (operational):
- Commit sizing: aim to cover P90 monthly GPU-hours in each region as committed reserved capacity. Buy burst buffer + autoscaling to cover P99–P99.9 peaks. This minimizes committed cost while keeping tail risk within a predictable burst budget.
- Cache investment: prioritize improving cacheability for medium/long requests—moving cache hit from 0.2 -> 0.4 is roughly equivalent to buying ~10–12% more committed GPUs in NA by cost savings.
- Quantization policy: enable quantized variants for medium models in EU+APAC first (where $/GPU-hour premiums are higher) to get highest $/1M token reduction per risk of quality regressions.
- Regional burst lanes: keep small reserved pools in neighboring regions with fast network egress (or edge peering) to handle 2–3 hour failover windows without forcing CPU fallback.

Open questions / TODOs (notes from the simulation runs):
- Verify real product request mix with product analytics team (current base arrival rates are heuristics). Action: link JIRA-ANALYTICS-219.
- Incorporate token-based pricing tiers and customer-level SLAs (per-route cost assignment). Need mapping between API routes and model mix.
- Replace simple Poisson arrival with renewal process that uses session-level correlation (we expect bursty sessions for chat workloads).
- Run longer horizon (quarterly) with growth ramps to quantify commit vs re-up economics.

Notes on unit-econ conversion (how $/1M tokens computed):
- Convert simulated GPU-hours to effective tokens served using per-model measured tokens/sec converted to tokens per GPU-hour (benchmarks per model family).
- Add infra overhead: scheduler, network egress, storage ~20% of GPU-hour cost (amortized).
- Apply regional price multipliers: NA base price (spot/commit mix blended), EU +8–12% pricing due to instance premiums, APAC -3–5% relative to NA depending on provider and spot availability.
- Include quantization discount: quantized variant has lower effective tokens/sec variance - measured separately and applied as a multiplier.

Conservative vs aggressive commit playbook (short):
- Conservative: commit P99 monthly hours in each region (higher fixed cost) but very low runout risk; appropriate for customers with hard SLAs.
- Balanced (recommended): commit P90 + burst pool sized to cover weekly P99.9 spikes (mix of reserved + autoscale + transient spot).
- Aggressive (PLG): commit P50, rely on autoscale and multi-region fallback; cheaper but increases CPU fallback risk and potential quality regressions during spikes.

Appendix (quick modeling notes):
- Monte Carlo: 10k draws, seedable for reproducibility. Key outputs tracked per-run: GPU-hours per region, fraction of requests hitting cached KV, fraction served by quantized variant, CPU-fallback minutes, and average latency distribution.
- Metrics to export for product teams: expected $/1M tokens by route, P95 latency, P99.9 GPU-hour demand, probability of CPU-fallback > 0.5% in a month.

Slack/Communication snippets (for quick sharing):
- "Running probabilistic sim: P90 commit + 30% burst buffer looks like the cheapest low-risk option for mid-market customers — will share CSV soon (JIRA-ENG-1428)."
- "Cache hit improvements are the cheapest lever per $/1M reduction; prioritizing that gives runway breathing room for Dedicated sales."

- Next step: integrate real route-level analytics and re-run sim to generate recommended committed purchase orders for Q1 renewals.
